docs.title: Run a heavy test once. Reuse the result safely everywhere
docs.text:
Aval signs a test result and ties it to the exact inputs it used. A job with the same inputs and a trusted signer skips the test.

  1. List the inputs. Write the files and tools your test reads in aval.yaml. Aval hashes them into one fingerprint.
  2. Run once, sign the result. On a miss the test runs. With --push, Aval signs the result and stores it in your OCI registry.
  3. Verify, then skip. Same fingerprint, trusted signer: the test is skipped. Anything else: the test runs.

A result that fails verification is a security event, never a quiet miss.

docs.title: Artifact format
docs.text: How Aval stores a result in an OCI registry, what it signs, and the JSON aval verify -o json prints. The Go types in pkg/evidence are the source of truth. The identifiers and JSON shapes below are frozen; see Versioning.

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
All constants live in pkg/evidence.

Constant Value Used for Status ArtifactType application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2 artifactType of the OCI manifest frozen ArtifactTypeFingerprint application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1 artifactType of the per-fingerprint anchor manifest frozen MediaTypeDSSE application/vnd.dsse.envelope.v1+json Media type of the signed DSSE envelope layer DSSE standard MediaTypeExecution application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2+json Media type of the raw predicate JSON, when carried on its own frozen PayloadType application/vnd.in-toto+json DSSE payloadType in-toto standard StatementType https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1 in-toto Statement _type in-toto standard PredicateType https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2 in-toto predicateType frozen SchemaVersion v2 Predicate schemaVersion frozen ReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 version of the verify report frozen RunRecordVersion aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1 version of a run record provisional ArtifactTypeRun application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1 artifactType of a run record manifest provisional MediaTypeRun application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1+json Media type of the run record layer provisional ArtifactTypeStats application/vnd.trianalab.aval.stats.v1 artifactType of the per-test stats anchor manifest provisional StatsReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/stats-report/v1 version of the aval stats --output json document provisional

The bundle layer uses the Sigstore media type application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json. Manifests carry the annotation io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint (informational, frozen: verification reads the fingerprint from the signed predicate); the stats anchor carries io.trianalab.aval.test (provisional) with the test id. The contract apiVersion and the aval-fingerprint/v1 manifest version are also frozen (see the table under Versioning).

docs.title: OCI layout
docs.text:
There is no Aval server or database. The registry is the only index.

flowchart LR
  tag[tag sha256-FP] --> anchor[fingerprint anchor]
  e1[execution manifest] -- subject --> anchor
  e2[execution manifest] -- subject --> anchor
  e1 --> layers[layers: DSSE envelope,<br>Sigstore bundle]
  stag[tag stats-TEST] --> sanchor[stats anchor]
  r1[run record] -- subject --> sanchor

Per fingerprint there is one anchor manifest, and one execution manifest per execution whose subject is the anchor, so the OCI 1.1 referrers API lists every execution for a fingerprint. The anchor is deterministic: its bytes, and so its digest, depend only on the fingerprint. It is tagged sha256-<fingerprint hex>.

Anchor manifest 
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
  "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1",
  "config": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
    "size": 2,
    "data": "e30="
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
      "size": 2,
      "data": "e30="
    }
  ],
  "annotations": {
    "io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint": "sha256:<fingerprint hex>"
  }
}
Execution manifest 
{
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
  "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2",
  "config": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.empty.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:44136fa355b3678a1146ad16f7e8649e94fb4fc21fe77e8310c060f61caaff8a",
    "size": 2,
    "data": "e30="
  },
  "layers": [
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.dsse.envelope.v1+json",
      "digest": "sha256:<envelope digest>",
      "size": 1834
    },
    {
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.dev.sigstore.bundle.v0.3+json",
      "digest": "sha256:<bundle digest>",
      "size": 4210
    }
  ],
  "subject": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:<anchor digest>",
    "size": 512
  },
  "annotations": {
    "io.trianalab.aval.fingerprint": "sha256:<fingerprint hex>"
  }
}
  • config: the OCI empty descriptor ({}).
  • layers: the signed DSSE envelope, then the Sigstore bundle. Push refuses an attestation without a valid bundle. Fetch treats a missing bundle or envelope, any other or repeated layer, a manifest that is not sha256-addressed, over 4 MiB, or not matching its digest as a verification failure.
  • subject: always the anchor of the execution's fingerprint. The tested revision or artifact is recorded inside the statement, not in the manifest, so the referrers of a tested image do not list its evidence.

docs.title: Push
docs.text:
• Push never replaces: identical bytes are a no-op, anything else adds a referrer. Re-tagging the deterministic anchor also repairs a moved tag.
  • Registries without the referrers API (GHCR): oras keeps the referrers tag schema index, which concurrent pushes can overwrite. Aval checks that the new digest is listed, re-pushing up to 3 times, 1 s apart; otherwise exit 1. A registry that indexes for longer than about 2 s, or more than 64 attestations, also makes the check fail. A dropped execution is never a candidate.
  • Push needs no DELETE rights.

docs.title: Lookup and consumption
docs.text:
1. Compute the fingerprint locally (aval run --fingerprint-only).
  2. Resolve the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex> in the --registry repository. It must point at the anchor digest Aval computes for that fingerprint; anything else is a verification failure (the tag was moved).
  3. List the anchor's execution referrers; each is a candidate, by digest. A malformed referrer entry is still a candidate, and fetching it fails verification, so it never turns into a miss.
  4. Fetch each candidate by digest (repo@sha256:...), never by tag.
  5. Verify each envelope and apply the trust policy.
Limit Value When exceeded candidates per fingerprint 64 error (the test runs) referrer listing requests 64 error manifest size 4 MiB verification-failed --registry-timeout 1m; lookup and fetch share it, push has its own; runner.command is never under it error a listed candidate returns 404 skipped with a warning; all gone: miss

A missing tag, or an anchor without executions, is a miss (evidence.ErrNotFound, exit 4). An artifact that exists but is malformed or fails signature or policy checks is a verification failure (evidence.ErrVerification, exit 5) and a security event.

docs.title: Registry credentials
docs.text:
Aval reads registry credentials the way Docker does: from $DOCKER_CONFIG/config.json, or ~/.docker/config.json when DOCKER_CONFIG is not set, including the credential helpers it names (credsStore, credHelpers, for example docker-credential-osxkeychain or docker-credential-ecr-login). Log in with docker login <registry> (or oras login, which writes the same file). Without an entry for the registry, Aval connects anonymously, which is enough to read a public repository.

A config file that cannot be parsed, or a helper that fails, is outcome error (exit 1): aval run runs the test and nothing is reused. Loopback registries (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) use plain HTTP; every other registry uses HTTPS.

docs.title: Multiple attestations per fingerprint
docs.text:
Every execution stays a referrer of the anchor, so a later push cannot hide an earlier one. aval verify verifies every candidate:

  • The verified candidate with the highest level wins; on a tie a non-passed result, then the lowest digest.
  • A candidate that cannot be checked (error) blocks reuse: it might have outranked the winner.
  • A signer below minTrustLevel is rejected as miss and does not block.
  • If nothing is reused: verification-failed beats error beats miss.

Unused candidates are listed in the report's rejected; any that failed verification add one aval: SECURITY: ... line on stderr.

docs.title: The 64-candidate cap and cleanup
docs.text:
Every push adds one execution, even for the same inputs (hostname and timestamps differ), and Aval never deletes one. Past 64 executions, every lookup for that fingerprint is error and the test always runs; every push still adds one, then exits 1. Other fingerprints are not affected, so the next input change also ends it.

Push from one place (for example CI on the main branch). aval run --push does not push after a reuse, but aval run --shadow --push pushes every time.

To clean up, list the executions and delete the ones you no longer need, for example with ORAS:

aval run --fingerprint-only            # prints sha256:<hex>
oras discover --artifact-type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2 <repo>:sha256-<hex>
oras manifest delete <repo>@sha256:<execution digest>

The registry must allow deletes (registry:2 needs REGISTRY_STORAGE_DELETE_ENABLED=true; on GHCR, delete the package versions). Deleting executions is safe: it can make a result stop being reusable, never make an untrusted one reusable. Keep any execution that failed verification until you have looked into it.

docs.title: Run records
docs.text:
aval run --record publishes one run record per run, for every outcome, so reuse can be measured from the registry alone. --record-file <path> writes the same record to a file, and aval record --record-file <path> publishes it later, for example from a job that has write credentials but runs no tests.

Records are statistics, never evidence: unsigned, and never read by aval run or aval verify, so a record, forged or not, cannot cause reuse, change an outcome or count toward the 64-candidate cap.

Recording never changes the exit code: a record that cannot be published or written is a warning (aval: warning: run record not ...). --record needs --registry. An existing --record-file that is not an Aval file is never overwritten. A run that stops before the lookup (bad flags, an invalid contract, --fingerprint-only) publishes no record.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Per test there is one stats anchor, separate from every fingerprint anchor. It is deterministic (its digest depends on the test id alone) and tagged stats-<test id> (registry.StatsTag); fingerprint tags and OCI referrers tag schema tags start with sha256-, so the tags cannot collide. It has the same shape as the fingerprint anchor, with "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.stats.v1" and the annotation "io.trianalab.aval.test": "<test id>".

Each record is an OCI 1.1 image manifest with "artifactType": "application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1", the empty config, one layer of media type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1+json holding the record JSON, and the stats anchor as subject. Records are listed by the stats anchor's referrers. Unlike registry.Push, publishing a record does not confirm the referrers listing, so on a registry without the referrers API two concurrent records for one test can drop one of them. On such registries all records of a test also share one referrers index, which grows with every record; once it exceeds the registry's manifest size limit, publishing a record fails with a warning; prune old records (see Pruning run records).

docs.title: Record JSON
docs.text:
evidence.RunRecord, parsed by evidence.ParseRunRecord:

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1. testId string always metadata.name from the contract. fingerprint string always sha256:<hex>; empty when the fingerprint could not be computed. outcome string always The lookup decision, as in the verify report. reused bool always true when a verified result was reused and the test did not run. With --shadow, or when --report cannot be written, it is false. result string when known The reused or the real passed / failed; omitted when runner.command could not start. verifiedResult string when outcome is verified The result of the verified attestation. With reused false and the test run (--shadow), a verifiedResult that differs from result is a false hit. Records made before it was added (#88) lack it. testDurationMs integer always How long runner.command ran, in milliseconds; 0 when it did not run. savedDurationMs integer always On reuse, the test duration recorded in the reused attestation (finishedAt - startedAt); 0 otherwise. avalVersion string always Version of the aval binary that ran. recordedAt RFC 3339 timestamp always When the record was made. ciRunUrl string when passed --ci-run-url, a link to the CI run. Aval does not derive it from any CI vendor. repository string when passed --repository on aval run (or aval record, which overrides the record's), the source repository, e.g. acme/orders. Aval does not derive it from any CI vendor. aval stats --by repository counts records without it (made before it was added, #88) as unknown. 
{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/run-record/v1",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "outcome": "verified",
  "reused": true,
  "result": "passed",
  "verifiedResult": "passed",
  "testDurationMs": 0,
  "savedDurationMs": 1184000,
  "avalVersion": "0.3.0",
  "recordedAt": "2026-11-06T09:00:00Z",
  "ciRunUrl": "https://ci.example.com/acme/orders/runs/42",
  "repository": "acme/orders"
}

evidence.ParseRunRecord rejects an inconsistent record: reused true with an outcome other than verified or a non-zero testDurationMs, and a verifiedResult without outcome verified. aval record refuses it and aval stats skips it.

docs.title: Statistics: aval stats
docs.text:
aval stats reads the run records of a repository and aggregates them on demand (flags: CLI reference). It writes nothing and needs only read access. Records are unsigned, so anyone with push access can skew the numbers; they never affect reuse. Registry data is untrusted, so reading is bounded:

Case Result a record that is unreadable, over 64 KiB, inconsistent or of another test skipped and counted in skipped more than 1000 records, or 64 pages in one listing aval: warning: stopped reading run records: ... and truncated a listing fails, or --registry-timeout passes exit 1 --since filters after reading: bounds, timeout and skipped cover every record listed

Records are fetched one at a time (about 0.7 s each on GHCR), so the default 1m timeout covers some 80 records; raise --registry-timeout or prune old records.

docs.title: Stats report JSON
docs.text:
aval stats --output json prints evidence.StatsReport:

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/stats-report/v1. registry string always The repository read. since RFC 3339 timestamp with --since Records made before it are left out (not counted, not skipped). total object always Run statistics over every test in tests. tests array always One {"testId", "stats"} per test with records, sorted by test id; [] when there are none. repositories array with --by repository One {"repository", "stats"} per source repository, sorted; records without a repository are under unknown. Omitted when there are no records. skipped integer always Records read but not counted (see above). truncated string when a bound was hit Which bound, e.g. more than 1000 run records.

Run statistics (total, tests[].stats, repositories[].stats); runs is the sum of reused, the three misses and verificationFailures:

Field Meaning runs Records counted. reused Records with reused true. hitRate reused / runs; 0 when runs is 0. misses.noTrustedResult Outcome miss: no trusted attestation, an unacknowledged mutable reference (Pin your dependencies) or --no-reuse. misses.error Outcome error: Aval could not decide. misses.verifiedNotReused Outcome verified with reused false: --shadow, or the --report file could not be written. verificationFailures Outcome verification-failed: security events, not misses. shadowFalseHits Of verifiedNotReused, the runs whose result differs from verifiedResult. Records without both are not counted. testDurationMs Sum of testDurationMs: time spent running tests. savedDurationMs Sum of savedDurationMs: test time reuse saved.

A negative duration in a record (a clock jump, or an edit) counts as 0, and duration sums stop at the largest int64 instead of wrapping. The golden file is pkg/evidence/testdata/stats-report-v1.golden.json.

docs.title: Pruning run records
docs.text:
Records accumulate: one per recorded run. Aval never deletes one. To keep aval stats below its read bound, and the referrers index of registries without the referrers API below their manifest size limit, delete old records, for example with ORAS:

oras discover --artifact-type application/vnd.trianalab.aval.run.v1 <repo>:stats-<test id>
oras manifest delete <repo>@sha256:<record digest>

oras discover --format json shows each record's digest; fetch one with oras manifest fetch and oras blob fetch to read its recordedAt. Deleting records only changes statistics: run records never affect reuse. The registry must allow deletes (see the 64-candidate cap and cleanup).

docs.title: DSSE envelope
docs.text:
The layer is a DSSE envelope (evidence.Envelope):

{
  "payloadType": "application/vnd.in-toto+json",
  "payload": "<base64 of the in-toto Statement JSON>",
  "signatures": [
    { "keyid": "", "sig": "<base64 signature>" }
  ]
}

Signed by sigstore-go (trust model).

docs.title: in-toto Statement
docs.text:
The envelope payload is an in-toto Statement v1 (evidence.Statement). Its subject is the same one recorded in predicate.subject. aval run writes the test id as name and the fingerprint as the digest:

{
  "_type": "https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1",
  "subject": [
    {
      "name": "orders-integration",
      "digest": { "sha256": "<fingerprint hex>" }
    }
  ],
  "predicateType": "https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2",
  "predicate": { "...": "see below" }
}

runner.identity is the host name (a claim; trust comes from the signer), runner.trustLevel is 0, and execution.environment holds os and arch plus the declared toolchain. Recording a git commit or image as the subject is milestone 3 work (TODO(milestone-3)).

docs.title: Predicate
docs.text:
evidence.Predicate, JSON tags exactly as below. Required fields are the ones checked by Predicate.Validate (called by evidence.Parse).

Field Type Required Meaning schemaVersion string yes, must be v2 Predicate schema version. subject object yes Tested revision/artifact. subject.name string yes e.g. git+https://github.com/acme/orders or an image reference. subject.digest map string to string yes, non-empty e.g. {"gitCommit": "..."} or {"sha256": "..."}. test object Test identity: what was checked, independent of inputs. test.id string yes metadata.name from aval.yaml. test.cacheability string Class declared in the contract: hermetic, controlled-environment, external-dependencies, non-deterministic. result string yes passed or failed. execution object This run: its inputs and conditions. execution.fingerprint string yes, sha256:<64 hex> Fingerprint over the declared inputs. execution.fingerprintVersion string Manifest format, e.g. aval-fingerprint/v1. execution.environment map string to string no (omitted when empty) Conditions of the run (toolchain, OS/arch). Only keys declared under environment.toolchain in aval.yaml are part of the fingerprint; anything else here is informational. execution.exitCode integer Exit code of runner.command. runner object Who produced the result, as claimed. runner.identity string yes Claimed producer identity. runner.issuer string no (omitted when empty) Claimed identity issuer, e.g. an OIDC issuer URL. runner.trustLevel integer 0 unknown, 1 developer, 2 runner, 3 isolated. startedAt RFC 3339 timestamp yes Execution start. finishedAt RFC 3339 timestamp yes, not before startedAt Execution end. annotations map string to string no (omitted when empty) Free third-party metadata. Aval never reads it.

The runner block is a claim: trust comes from the verified signer and the policy, never from it. The Go fields Runner.Issuer, Runner.TrustLevel and Verification.TrustLevel are deprecated.

evidence.Parse only checks structure. A parsed predicate is a claim, not evidence; use evidence.Verify to get something you can rely on.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text: Keys use reverse-DNS of the owner, e.g. com.example.team, com.acme.ticket. Aval does not define, validate or interpret any key. Do not put secrets there: the predicate is published to the registry.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
{
  "schemaVersion": "v2",
  "subject": {
    "name": "orders-integration",
    "digest": { "sha256": "3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7" }
  },
  "test": {
    "id": "orders-integration",
    "cacheability": "controlled-environment"
  },
  "result": "passed",
  "execution": {
    "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
    "fingerprintVersion": "aval-fingerprint/v1",
    "environment": {
      "go": "1.25",
      "os": "linux",
      "arch": "amd64"
    },
    "exitCode": 0
  },
  "runner": {
    "identity": "ci-runner-7",
    "trustLevel": 0
  },
  "startedAt": "2026-11-05T10:12:03Z",
  "finishedAt": "2026-11-05T10:31:47Z",

    "com.acme.team": "payments"
  }
}

docs.title: Verify report
docs.text:
aval verify --output json prints one evidence.Report to stdout, and aval run --report <file> writes the same document for its lookup decision. This is the stable machine interface for CI scripts and external tools.

Field Type Present Meaning version string always aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1. outcome string always See outcomes below. testId string always metadata.name from the contract. fingerprint string always Locally computed sha256:<hex>. reference string when an attestation was found Immutable repo@sha256:<manifest digest>. result string verified only passed or failed from the verified predicate. signer object verified only Accepted policy identity that matched (issuer, subjectRegexp, trustLevel) plus the identity the signature actually carried: subject, the certificate subject (SAN) for keyless signatures, or keyId, base64(sha256(DER public key)) for key-based ones. subject and keyId are omitted when empty. predicate object verified only Full verified predicate. reason string non-verified outcomes Human-readable cause. rejected array when a candidate was not used Each {reference, outcome, reason}; outcome is verification-failed, error or miss. A verification-failed entry is a security event even when outcome is verified: alert. A miss entry is an authentic attestation whose signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel: routine non-reuse, no alert.

Outcomes:

outcome Meaning What the caller does verified Valid attestation satisfies the policy. Reuse result. miss No attestation for this fingerprint that the policy can reuse: none found, or only authentic ones whose signer the policy lists below minTrustLevel. Run the test. verification-failed Attestation exists but fails signature or policy. Run the test and alert. Never hide this. error Aval could not decide (registry unreachable, bad policy file, trusted root unavailable). Treat as a miss: run the test (fail closed).

aval verify exits with the outcome (exit codes); aval run acts on it and exits with the test result (Outcomes).

  • A fingerprint error: aval verify prints no report and exits 1; aval run --report writes outcome error with an empty fingerprint, then runs the test. Bad flags or an invalid contract: no report, exit 2.
  • No --policy, or a non-deterministic contract: miss, no lookup.
  • A policy, or a trusted root a candidate needs, that cannot load: error.

Example (verified):

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1",
  "outcome": "verified",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "reference": "ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval@sha256:8c1d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0",
  "result": "passed",
  "signer": {
    "issuer": "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    "subjectRegexp": "^https://github.com/acme/orders/\\.github/workflows/ci\\.yaml@refs/heads/main$",
    "trustLevel": 2,
    "subject": "https://github.com/acme/orders/.github/workflows/ci.yaml@refs/heads/main"
  },
  "predicate": { "...": "as in the predicate example" }
}

Example (miss):

{
  "version": "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1",
  "outcome": "miss",
  "testId": "orders-integration",
  "fingerprint": "sha256:3f9a7c2e1b4d5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c4d5e6f7",
  "reason": "no attestation found for fingerprint"
}

docs.title: Versioning and compatibility
docs.text:
These rules apply to every frozen format:

Format Version identifiers (move together) Frozen at Statement and predicate PredicateType, SchemaVersion, MediaTypeExecution, ArtifactType .../execution/v2, v2, execution.v2 Fingerprint anchor ArtifactTypeFingerprint fingerprint.v1 Verify report, outcomes and exit codes ReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 Run record and stats anchor RunRecordVersion, ArtifactTypeRun, MediaTypeRun, ArtifactTypeStats run-record/v1, run.v1, stats.v1 (provisional) Stats report StatsReportVersion aval.trianalab.io/stats-report/v1 (provisional) Contract and policy file apiVersion aval.trianalab.io/v1 Fingerprint manifest header line, execution.fingerprintVersion aval-fingerprint/v1

The predicate keeps v2: v1 was used before and an identifier is never recycled, and v2 is already under aval.trianalab.io and is what v0.1.0 writes, so attestations published by v0.1.0 stay readable. The report and the contract moved from the pre-freeze aval.dev/.../v1alpha1 names to aval.trianalab.io at v1. There is no accept window for the old names: a contract or policy file with aval.dev/v1alpha1 is invalid.

docs.title: Additive changes (same identifier)
docs.text:
• A new optional field, omitted when empty, whose absence means what it meant before.
  • A new key under annotations.
  • A new optional contract field. Older aval binaries reject a contract that uses it (unknown fields are rejected), which fails closed.
  • A new manifest section that only a new optional contract field brings. Every contract without the field keeps its manifest byte for byte, and a contract with it cannot have had a fingerprint before, so no fingerprint changes meaning.

Existing fields keep their name, JSON tag, type and meaning.

docs.title: Breaking changes (new identifier)
docs.text:
• Renaming or removing a field, changing its type or its meaning.
  • Making an optional field required, or tightening validation of an existing one.
  • A new value of a closed set: outcome, result, trustLevel, cacheability class, or an exit code.
  • A change to what the fingerprint covers or how it is hashed: a new aval-fingerprint/vN. There is no accept window: old attestations become misses, never false hits.

A new predicate version changes PredicateType, SchemaVersion, MediaTypeExecution and ArtifactType together (execution/v3, execution.v3). Old and new artifacts can coexist in one repository.

docs.title: How consumers treat versions
docs.text:
• Unknown version: not evidence. Reject a predicateType, schemaVersion, report version or artifactType you do not know, and run the test. evidence.Verify does this for predicates.
  • Unknown fields: ignore them within a version you know. Do not decode Aval documents strictly. evidence.Parse ignores unknown fields.
  • Unknown values of a closed set: fail closed. An outcome other than the four listed above, a result other than passed or failed, or an unknown trust level or cacheability class means "not verified": run the test. Within a version such a value can only come from a bug or tampering.
  • No field grants trust. Trust comes from the verified signer and the policy (see trust-model.md), never from a field that is new or that you do not understand.

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text: Aval writes only the newest version of each format. When a breaking change mints a new version, the release notes say whether Aval keeps reading the old one for a transition. If it does, the old parser stays next to the new one, dispatching on the identifier, and old documents get no more trust than new ones; any identifier Aval does not know fails closed. Ending a transition is announced in the release notes of the release that removes it.

docs.title: Golden files
docs.text: pkg/evidence/testdata/*.golden.json set every field of the statement, predicate, verify report, run record and stats report, and only grow: an additive change adds its field to the golden of its version, and a new version adds a new file. The tests that enforce this: CONTRIBUTING.md.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
History
  • Predicate v1 became v2 when the execution manifest's subject changed from the tested artifact to the fingerprint anchor and the Sigstore bundle layer was added. Aval no longer reads or writes v1: a v1 artifact is never a candidate.
  • At the freeze (#17), the verify report moved from aval.dev/verify-report/v1alpha1 to aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1 and the contract and policy apiVersion from aval.dev/v1alpha1 to aval.trianalab.io/v1; every fingerprint changed, so older results are misses and the tests run once.
  • Within verify-report/v1 (#65), a signer below minTrustLevel became miss instead of verification-failed, and rejected[].outcome may be miss. No new value, field or exit code, so the version stays.
  • Within the provisional run-record/v1 (#88), records gained verifiedResult and repository, and inconsistent records are rejected; no record aval writes is affected.
  • Within aval-fingerprint/v1 (#102), scope.resolve adds resolve lines after the env lines; manifests without it are unchanged.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text: • 0148c76: Formats are frozen. The contract and policy apiVersion is now aval.trianalab.io/v1 and the verify report version is aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1; aval.dev/v1alpha1 contracts and policy files are rejected, so change that line in yours. The contract hash covers apiVersion, so results published before are misses and each test runs once. The predicate type (https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2), media and artifact types (application/vnd.trianalab.aval.execution.v2, application/vnd.trianalab.aval.fingerprint.v1) and predicate schemaVersion v2 are unchanged and now frozen, so attestations written by v0.1.0 keep a valid, readable format. Compatibility rules (additive changes within a version, what needs a new version, how consumers treat unknown fields and values, deprecation) are in docs/artifact-format.md, and golden files guard the JSON shape of the statement, predicate and verify report.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text:
• c17dc26: aval run and aval verify escape newlines and control characters in reasons printed as text and on stderr, so text from an untrusted attestation cannot start a log line of its own. Aval's own CI now reuses its signed e2e results, and a release requires a verified e2e attestation for its commit.
  • 59b9b66: pkg/evidence is semver-stable Go API: within a major version it changes additively only, and CI fails when an exported identifier is removed or changes type or signature without a new major module path. examples/evidence-consumer is a separate module that consumes Aval evidence through pkg/evidence alone, with its own signature verifier. The policy is in docs/integrations.md.
  • bbf9e55: Fingerprinting fails closed in two more cases: a scope.source glob that matches no file (a typo, or a name that differs on disk by case or Unicode form), and a file excluded only because a trailing ** in exclude matched zero segments (build/** against a file named build). Trees that fingerprinted before and still do keep the same fingerprint. A table-driven false-hit corpus now pins every kind of relevant and irrelevant change.

docs.title: Minor Changes
docs.text: • a6d2b1a: First release: signed aval binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows with checksums, SBOMs and SLSA provenance. aval --version prints the release version.

docs.title: Patch Changes
docs.text: • 59664a3: Dependency updates: oras.land/oras-go/v2 2.6.4 to 2.7.0; GitHub Actions actions/checkout to v7.0.1, actions/setup-go to v7.0.0, actions/upload-artifact to v7.0.2, actions/download-artifact to v8.0.2 and actions/dependency-review-action to v5.0.0 (Node 24 runtime).

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Every command, flag and exit code.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code aval run aval verify aval push 0 the test passed, or a verified passing result was reused a verified result exists (passing or failing) pushed 1 error (the test still runs when it can), or a false hit in --shadow error: registry, policy, trusted root or fingerprint error: signing, registry or a result that does not match the current inputs 2 bad flags or invalid aval.yaml bad flags or invalid aval.yaml bad flags or invalid aval.yaml 3 the test failed, or a verified failing result was reused not used not used 4 not used: a miss runs the test miss: no result the policy can reuse not used 5 verification failed, after running the test: a security event verification failed: a security event not used 6 reserved, never returned reserved, never returned reserved, never returned

A miss (4) is routine. A verification failure (5) means someone published a result the policy does not trust; never hide it or retry it away.

docs.title: aval
docs.text:
Verifiable test execution reuse: signed test results as OCI artifacts

Usage:
  aval [flags]
  aval [command]

Available Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command
  push        Sign and publish a recorded execution result
  record      Publish a run record written by 'aval run --record-file'
  run         Reuse a verified result for the current inputs, or run the test
  stats       Aggregate the run records in the registry: reuse, misses, time saved
  verify      Check whether a trusted result exists for the current inputs

Flags:
  -h, --help      help for aval
  -v, --version   version for aval

Use "aval [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: aval completion
docs.text:
Generate the autocompletion script for aval for the specified shell. See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

Usage:
  aval completion [command]

Available Commands:
  bash        Generate the autocompletion script for bash
  fish        Generate the autocompletion script for fish
  powershell  Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
  zsh         Generate the autocompletion script for zsh

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for completion

Use "aval completion [command] --help" for more information about a command.

docs.title: aval push
docs.text:
push signs the result recorded by 'aval run' and publishes it. The result must be for the current inputs: same test id, cacheability and fingerprint. Keyless signing reads the OIDC token from $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN.

Usage:
  aval push [flags]

Flags:
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
  -h, --help                        help for push
      --key string                  signing key path (default: keyless OIDC)
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations (required)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --result string               result recorded by 'aval run' (default ".aval/result.json")

docs.title: aval record
docs.text:
record publishes a run record that 'aval run --record-file' wrote, as 'aval run --record' would have. Use it to publish, from a job with write credentials that runs no tests, the record of a run made without them. Run records are unsigned statistics: run and verify never read them. --repository sets the record's source repository.

Usage:
  aval record [flags]

Flags:
  -h, --help                        help for record
      --record-file string          run record written by 'aval run --record-file' (required)
      --registry string             OCI repository for run records (required)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --repository string           source repository (e.g. acme/orders); default: the one in the record

docs.title: aval run
docs.text:
run computes the fingerprint, looks up a signed result and reuses it if the trust policy accepts it. Otherwise it runs runner.command, records the result (--result) and, with --push, signs and publishes it.

Anything Aval cannot prove runs the test. A verification failure runs the test and exits 5: a security event. --shadow runs the test even after a verified result and exits 1 if they disagree (a false hit).

--record publishes a run record for statistics; a failure is only a warning. --record-file writes it to a file for 'aval record'.

Exit codes: 0 pass, 3 fail, 5 verification failed, 1 error or false hit, 2 usage. Keyless signing reads $SIGSTORE_ID_TOKEN; runner.command never sees it.

Usage:
  aval run [flags]

Flags:
      --ci-run-url string           link to the CI run, stored in the run record
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
      --explain                     print the fingerprint manifest (what was hashed)
      --fingerprint-only            print the execution fingerprint and exit
  -h, --help                        help for run
      --key string                  signing key path for --push (default: keyless OIDC)
      --no-reuse                    always run, never reuse
      --policy string               trust policy file (required for reuse; without it the test always runs)
      --push                        sign and publish the result after running (needs --registry)
      --record                      publish a run record for statistics after the run (needs --registry; best-effort)
      --record-file string          also write the run record to this file, for 'aval record'
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations, e.g. ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (lookup and fetch share one; push has its own) (default 1m0s)
      --report string               also write the lookup decision as a verify report (JSON) to this file
      --repository string           source repository (e.g. acme/orders), stored in the run record for 'aval stats --by repository'
      --result string               where to record the result for 'aval push' (default ".aval/result.json")
      --shadow                      verify, but run the test anyway and fail on a false hit

docs.title: aval stats
docs.text:
stats reads the run records that 'aval run --record' and 'aval record' published to the registry and aggregates them: runs, hit rate, misses by cause, verification failures, shadow false hits, and total and saved test time, per test (or per source repository with --by repository) and in total. It reads every test with a stats anchor, or only --test. It writes nothing, locally or to the registry.

Run records are unsigned statistics and never affect reuse. Unreadable or invalid records are skipped and counted. Reading stops after 1000 records or 64 pages per listing; prune old records. Raise --registry-timeout for many records.

--since keeps records made at or after a time: a duration back from now (168h, 30d) or a date (2026-11-01, or RFC 3339).

Exit codes: 0 statistics printed, 1 error (registry), 2 usage.

Usage:
  aval stats [flags]

Flags:
      --by string                   group by test or repository (the run record's source repository) (default "test")
  -h, --help                        help for stats
  -o, --output string               output format: text or json (default "text")
      --registry string             OCI repository holding the run records (required)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)
      --since string                only records made since: a duration (168h, 30d) or a date (2026-11-01, RFC 3339)
      --test string                 only this test id (metadata.name); default: every test with run records

docs.title: aval verify
docs.text:
verify computes the fingerprint, looks up the attestation and verifies its signature and the trust policy, without running anything.

Exit codes: 0 verified, 4 miss, 5 verification failed (security event), 1 error (registry, policy or fingerprint), 2 usage or invalid aval.yaml.

Usage:
  aval verify [flags]

Flags:
  -f, --contract string             path to the test contract (default "aval.yaml")
  -h, --help                        help for verify
  -o, --output string               output format: text or json (default "text")
      --policy string               trust policy file (without it every lookup is a miss)
      --registry string             OCI repository for attestations (required)
      --registry-timeout duration   deadline for this command's registry calls (default 1m0s)

docs.title: The test contract: aval.yaml
docs.text: aval.yaml says what a test is, how to run it and which files it reads. Aval reuses a result only when those declared inputs are identical. An input you do not declare is invisible to Aval. Format: aval.trianalab.io/v1, frozen (Versioning).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1   # required, exact value
kind: Test                      # required, exact value

metadata:
  name: orders-integration      # test identity: WHAT is checked

runner:
  # argv, executed without a shell. Order matters and is part of the fingerprint.
  command: ["go", "test", "-tags=integration", "./orders/..."]

scope:
  source:                       # required, each glob must match >= 1 file
    - "orders/**/*.go"
    - "internal/**/*.go"
    - "testdata/orders/**"
  exclude:                      # optional, removes files selected by source
    - "**/*_bench_test.go"
  dependencies:                 # optional, each glob must match >= 1 file
    - "go.mod"
    - "go.sum"
  allowMutable:                 # optional, accepts a mutable reference on purpose
    - ref: "postgres:16"
      reason: "rebuilt and scanned nightly"

environment:
  toolchain:                    # optional, declared, not detected (v0)
    go: "1.25"
  env:                          # optional, names only; values are hashed
    - CGO_ENABLED
    - GOFLAGS

cacheability: hermetic          # required, see "Cacheability classes"

Check it locally:

aval run -f path/to/aval.yaml --fingerprint-only   # prints sha256:<hex>
aval run -f path/to/aval.yaml --explain --fingerprint-only   # also prints the manifest

Diff the --explain output of two machines to see which file, toolchain entry or variable differs. -f defaults to ./aval.yaml; the root is always the contract file's directory.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
• Unknown fields and files with more than one YAML document are rejected (exit 2), so a typo like sorce: fails instead of shrinking the scope.
  • Every field is part of the fingerprint.
Field Type Required Rules apiVersion string yes Must be aval.trianalab.io/v1. kind string yes Must be Test. metadata.name string yes 1-64 chars of [a-z0-9._-], starting and ending with [a-z0-9]. runner.command list of strings yes Non-empty argv, first element not blank. No shell. scope.source list of globs yes At least one glob. Each glob must match a file, and at least one file must remain after exclude. scope.exclude list of globs no Removes files from the source set (not from dependencies). May match nothing. scope.dependencies list of globs no Lockfiles and manifests. Each glob must match a file. scope.allowMutable list of {file, ref, reason} no Accepts a mutable reference on purpose: ref exactly as Aval reports it, plus a non-blank reason. An optional file (relative to the contract, or runner.command) limits it to that file; without file, a ref that several files report is not accepted. See Pin your dependencies. scope.resolve list of kind: reference no One kind: reference per entry. Kind is one of image, npm, pypi, go, maven, crate, gem, git, url. The reference must not contain credentials. See Resolve references. scope.contracts list of paths no Other contracts this test depends on (Depend on another part of the repo). Each path is relative to this contract's directory: clean (.. only at the start), slash-separated, no spaces, ending in .yaml or .yml, listed once. At fingerprint time the file must be a valid contract inside the git working tree of this contract (the nearest directory at or above it with a .git entry), with no symlink on the path; if this contract's own directory is a symlink, .. is resolved from its real location. No cycles, at most 8 levels and 64 distinct contracts. A referenced contract's mutable references block reuse here too, unless its own scope.allowMutable accepts them. environment.toolchain map string to string no Keys match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$. Values are not validated. environment.env list of strings no Variable names matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. cacheability string yes One of hermetic, controlled-environment, external-dependencies, non-deterministic.

docs.title: Globs
docs.text:
scope.source, scope.exclude and scope.dependencies use the same globs:

Glob Matches src/**/*.go src/a.go and src/x/y/a.go *.go top-level files only: * does not cross / dir/** every file under dir; globs never match directories ** every file Rejected /a, ./a, ../a, a//b, a\b, foo**, **.go, [a-
  • Relative to the contract's directory; a glob cannot escape it.
  • Case-sensitive and byte-exact: Makefile is not makefile, NFC is not NFD.
  • Order does not matter.

docs.title: Test identity vs execution fingerprint
docs.text: metadata.name says what is checked. The fingerprint says with which inputs. Renaming a test changes its fingerprint.

docs.title: Cacheability classes
docs.text:
Class Use it when Reused hermetic the test reads only the declared files yes controlled-environment it uses services you pin, such as a Compose image by digest yes external-dependencies it calls something you do not control only if the policy allows it non-deterministic the same inputs can give a different result never

A reusable class still needs a signed result your policy trusts. A non-deterministic test is never looked up. A hermetic or controlled-environment test with a mutable reference that allowMutable does not accept is a miss, and its result is not published (Pin your dependencies).

docs.title: What goes into the fingerprint
docs.text:
The fingerprint is sha256:<hex> of a line-oriented manifest (format aval-fingerprint/v1). aval run --explain prints the exact text that was hashed, in this order:

aval-fingerprint/v1
contract <sha256 of canonical contract JSON>
source <sha256> <mode> <path>
dependency <sha256> <mode> <path>
toolchain <key>=<value>
env <NAME> <sha256 of value | unset>
resolve <kind> <reference> <version> <immutable id>
contract <path> <name> <fingerprint>
Line Holds Not affected by header aval-fingerprint/v1, bumped when an existing contract's manifest would change contract sha256 of the parsed contract as JSON comments, formatting, key order, the order and duplicates of set-like lists (argv order counts; an empty list equals an omitted one) source, dependency sha256 of the content, x (any exec bit) or -, path. A file in both sets appears twice owner, timestamps, other permission bits toolchain key=value as written; not checked against the installed tools env sha256 of the value, or unset (empty is not unset); values never appear in clear resolve kind, reference, version or floating, immutable id; only with scope.resolve, and needs the network (Resolve references) the registry address contract <path> one line per scope.contracts entry: the path as written, the referenced contract's metadata.name and its fingerprint, computed from its own directory and inputs (so references are transitive). --explain also prints the tree, one depends on <path> (<name>) <fingerprint> line per reference

Lines are sorted within each section, so checkout path and walk order do not matter. Paths are hashed byte for byte. Windows has no exec bit, so an executable file fingerprints differently there than on Unix.

docs.title: What does not go in
docs.text: Not hashed Note files no source or dependencies glob matches the main risk: keep the scope honest .git directories exact name; a regular .git file is hashed .aval/ directories and the command's --result/--report files so ["**"] stays stable; keep them under .aval/. A path in scope that holds a real input exits 2. In a scope.contracts reference they stay inputs (a miss, never a false hit) commit, branch, VCS metadata two commits with the same scope share a result environment variables not in environment.env the real toolchain, OS and architecture unless declared

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
Declared scope means some changes are invisible by design. A test that depends on one of these can reuse a result it should not:

  • a file the test reads that scope does not match, including a case or Unicode mismatch under a wildcard glob
  • an environment variable the test reads that environment.env does not list
  • content behind a name the scanner does not recognize, or a network service: use scope.resolve or external-dependencies
  • the installed toolchain, OS and architecture

Mitigation: review the contract, use aval run --shadow, pick the right cacheability class.

docs.title: Fail-closed errors
docs.text:
Aval cannot prove the inputs: aval run reports outcome error, runs the test and records nothing; --fingerprint-only, --explain, aval verify and aval push exit 1.

Message Fix source glob "<glob>" matched no files fix the glob; a case or Unicode mismatch also matches nothing scope.source matched no files exclude removed every source file source "<path>" is excluded only by a trailing "**" exclude it by name, or narrow the glob dependency glob "<glob>" matched no files fix the glob only regular files are supported in scope remove the symlink, device or socket from scope "<path>" is a symlink a glob could match files under symlinks are not followed, and exclude does not lift this; the contract directory itself may be a symlink control characters in path are not supported rename the file (newline or carriage return) resolve <kind> <reference>: <reason> see When resolution fails scope.contracts <path>: <reason> any error above in the referenced contract, or: missing or invalid contract, leads outside the repository root, no git working tree (.git) at or above <dir>, <path> is a symlink, <path> is not a regular file, cycle: a/aval.yaml -> b/aval.yaml -> a/aval.yaml, more than 8 levels or 64 contracts any I/O error while walking or reading make the file or directory readable; the walk only enters directories a glob can match

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text:
aval.trianalab.io/v1 is frozen; policy files use the same value. Within v1 the schema only gets new optional fields. An older aval rejects a field it does not know, which fails closed.

aval.dev/v1alpha1 is rejected: change that line. Rules: artifact format.

docs.title: Future work
docs.text:
• Detected toolchain: verify or record the installed toolchain instead of trusting environment.toolchain. Not scheduled in milestones 1-5.
  • Observed inputs: trace which files the test actually reads, to flag undeclared inputs or suggest scope. v0 never infers scope.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: One static binary for Linux, macOS and Windows (amd64, arm64), from GitHub Releases. The installers check the download before they install it.

docs.title: Linux and macOS
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash

Installs into /usr/local/bin, with sudo only if that directory is not writable. Needs curl or wget, and sha256sum or shasum. Works with the bash 3.2 that macOS ships.

Variable Flag Windows Effect DESIRED_VERSION=v0.2.0 --version v0.2.0 yes install this release, not the latest AVAL_INSTALL_DIR=<dir> yes install here USE_SUDO=false --no-sudo no never use sudo AVAL_NO_VERIFY=1 --no-verify yes skip the cosign and gh checks (sha256 still runs) AVAL_DOWNLOAD_URL=<url> yes download from a mirror; the signer stays pinned

Piped, pass flags after bash -s --:

curl -fsSL https://aval.run/install.sh | bash -s -- --version v0.2.0

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
In PowerShell 5.1 or 7:

irm https://aval.run/install.ps1 | iex

Installs aval.exe into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\aval and adds it to your user PATH, without admin rights. Settings: the variables marked Windows above.

docs.title: What the installers check
docs.text:
Check Runs the archive's sha256 matches checksums.txt always checksums.txt has a Sigstore signature from Aval's release workflow at that tag if cosign is on PATH the archive matches the release's SLSA provenance if gh 2.49 or later is on PATH (no login)

A failed check installs nothing. A check that cannot run is reported.

docs.title: By hand
docs.text:
Download the archive, checksums.txt and the signatures, check them, then put aval on your PATH:

VERSION=0.2.0
OS=linux        # or darwin
ARCH=amd64      # or arm64
BASE=https://github.com/TrianaLab/aval/releases/download/v$VERSION
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/aval_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/checksums.txt"
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/checksums.txt.sigstore.json"
curl -fsSLO "$BASE/provenance.sigstore.json"
cosign verify-blob checksums.txt --bundle checksums.txt.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity "https://github.com/TrianaLab/aval/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/v$VERSION"
sha256sum --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt   # macOS: shasum -a 256 --ignore-missing -c checksums.txt
gh attestation verify "aval_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz" --bundle provenance.sigstore.json --repo TrianaLab/aval
tar -xzf "aval_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz" aval
sudo mv aval /usr/local/bin/

docs.title: From source
docs.text: go install github.com/TrianaLab/aval/cmd/aval@latest. The binary reports version dev and has no release checks.

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: Delete /usr/local/bin/aval (or your AVAL_INSTALL_DIR), or %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\aval on Windows and remove it from your user PATH.

docs.title: Consume evidence
docs.text: Three surfaces are stable: the OCI artifact, the Go package pkg/evidence, and aval verify -o json. Nothing else (internal packages, CLI text output, the manifest layout) is a contract. The formats are frozen (compatibility rules).

docs.title: 1. OCI artifact and predicate
docs.text: A result is an in-toto v1 Statement in a DSSE envelope, found through the tag sha256-<fingerprint hex> and the OCI 1.1 referrers of the manifest it points at, and consumed by digest. Predicate type https://aval.trianalab.io/attestation/execution/v2; fields and layout: artifact format.

docs.title: 2. Go package github.com/TrianaLab/aval/pkg/evidence
docs.text:
pkg/evidence has no dependency on the rest of the module and is the only public Go API:

Symbol Purpose Parse(data []byte) (*Predicate, error) decode predicate JSON and run Validate; no signature check (*Predicate).Validate() error structural checks: schemaVersion == "v2", subject, test.id, result, fingerprint format, runner.identity, timestamps Verify(ctx, *Envelope, VerifyOptions) (*Verification, error) check the signature, match the signer against the policy, enforce the minimum level, decode the statement, require the expected fingerprint, test id and a reusable cacheability; every failure is a *VerificationError SignatureVerifier, Signer checks a signature cryptographically and returns the signer it binds, with no policy. pkg/evidence ships no implementation, to stay free of Sigstore; a public Sigstore one is planned for milestone 5 MatchIdentity(ids, issuer, subject) (Identity, bool) the keyless identity that grants a signer the highest level; SubjectRegexp matches the whole subject MatchSigner(ids, Signer) (Identity, bool) MatchIdentity for keyless signers, PublicKey entries for key signers PublicKeyID(pem) (string, error) base64(sha256(DER)) of a PEM public key, the key hint in key-based bundles VerifyOptions expected fingerprint and test id, accepted Identities, MinTrustLevel, AllowedCacheability, Signature (required) ErrNotFound no attestation for the fingerprint: a miss, run the test ErrVerification an attestation failed signature or policy checks: a security event Report, ReportVersion the document aval verify --output json prints RunRecord, RunRecordVersion, ParseRunRecord a run record (run records); unsigned statistics, never a basis for trust StatsReport, TestStats, RepositoryStats, RunStats, MissCauses, StatsReportVersion, StatsUnknownRepository the document aval stats --output json prints (stats report)

ExpectedFingerprint and ExpectedTestID come from your local contract, never from the attestation; both are required and must equal the predicate's execution.fingerprint and test.id. Levels are numbers in reports: 0 unknown, 1 developer, 2 runner, 3 isolated (trust model).

A complete consumer that imports only pkg/evidence: Consume from Go. ErrNotFound comes from your lookup step, not from Verify.

docs.title: Go API compatibility
docs.text:
pkg/evidence follows semantic versioning as part of the module github.com/TrianaLab/aval. Within a major version its exported API changes additively only: new identifiers, new struct fields that keep a comparable struct comparable, new methods on concrete types. Anything else (removing or renaming, changing a type or signature, adding a method to an exported interface) needs a new module path, github.com/TrianaLab/aval/v2. The exported surface is snapshotted in pkg/evidence/testdata/api-v1.txt and checked in CI.

The Go API and the wire formats are versioned separately: a breaking format change gets a new identifier, and supporting it is an additive Go change.

docs.title: 3. aval verify --output json
docs.text:
aval verify computes the fingerprint, looks up the attestation, verifies it against the trust policy and runs nothing. With -o json it prints the verify report on stdout; stderr adds one aval: SECURITY: ... line when an attestation failed verification. Exit 2 prints no report, and neither does exit 1 when fingerprinting failed (exit codes).

CI snippet that keeps miss and verification failure apart:

set +e
report=$(aval verify --registry ghcr.io/acme/orders-aval --policy aval-policy.yaml -o json)
code=$?
set -e

outcome=$(jq -r '.outcome // "error"' <<<"$report")
case "$code:$outcome" in
  0:verified)
    if jq -e '[.rejected[]? | select(.outcome == "verification-failed")] | length > 0' <<<"$report" >/dev/null; then
      ./notify-security.sh "$report" # a rejected candidate failed verification
    fi
    echo "reusing $(jq -r .reference <<<"$report") (result: $(jq -r .result <<<"$report"))"
    [ "$(jq -r .result <<<"$report")" = passed ] || exit 1
    ;;
  4:miss)
    echo "no attestation for $(jq -r .fingerprint <<<"$report"), running test"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
  5:verification-failed)
    echo "::error::untrusted attestation for $(jq -r .testId <<<"$report"): $(jq -r .reason <<<"$report")"
    ./notify-security.sh "$report"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
  *)
    echo "aval could not decide (exit $code), running test"
    ./run-tests.sh
    ;;
esac

Check both the exit code and outcome; if they disagree, treat it as error.

docs.title: Guidance
docs.text:
• Always verify. Parse and Validate only check structure; a parsed predicate is a claim, and runner.identity is self-reported.
  • Pin versions. Check schemaVersion == "v2" on predicates (Validate does this) and version == "aval.trianalab.io/verify-report/v1" on reports. Reject versions you do not know. Within a version, ignore unknown fields.
  • Treat verification-failed as a security event, fail closed, consume by digest and never widen cacheability: see fail closed.
  • Your metadata goes in annotations with reverse-DNS keys (dev.pacto.service). Aval never reads them and will not add consumer fields.

docs.title: Pin your dependencies
docs.text:
Goal: no input that can change behind the same name.

Aval hashes the text postgres:16, not the image behind it, so a repushed tag would not change the fingerprint. Aval reports such mutable references, in the scope and in runner.command, and does not reuse a result that depends on one:

mutable: compose.yaml:3 (container) postgres:16: a tag can be repushed: pin the image by digest (name:tag@sha256:...)

The fix is the immutable id in the file:

image: redis:7.4-alpine@sha256:c5d34a98396a4775e223c74e929162c35c5a2182901ba26b50ade939941ce14b

flowchart LR
  f([finding]) --> c{cacheability}
  c -- "hermetic,<br>controlled-environment" --> m([miss, nothing published]):::muted
  c -- external-dependencies --> p([printed only])
  c -- non-deterministic --> n([never reused anyway])

aval verify exits 4; aval run --push and aval push publish nothing. The line names file:line, ecosystem, the reference and the fix. --fingerprint-only prints it on stderr.

How the scan works
  • It reads files only; it never fetches, resolves or runs anything.
  • At most 1 MiB per file. A bigger or unreadable file it should check is a scan finding that cannot be accepted: shrink or split it.
  • Lockfiles (pnpm-lock.yaml, go.sum, Cargo.lock, ...) are hashed, not scanned.

docs.title: Fix it by ecosystem
docs.text:
Ecosystem Commit and add to scope.dependencies In files and commands, pin Go go.sum go install x@v0.30.0, not @latest or @main JavaScript a lockfile (package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lock or bun.lockb); without one every range is reported npm ci, npx --yes prettier@3.3.3 Python requirements with == (better with hashes), or poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, uv.lock, pdm.lock git requirements @<40-hex>; files named by -r/-c must be in scope Rust Cargo.lock (workspace root) cargo install tool --version 1.2.3 Maven, Gradle no SNAPSHOT, LATEST, RELEASE, 1.+, latest.release or ranges in pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts), *.versions.toml Ruby, PHP Gemfile.lock (or gems.locked), composer.lock gem install tool --version 1.2.3 OS packages apt-get install curl=8.5.0-2, apk add jq=1.7.1-r0, dnf/yum/microdnf install curl-7.76.1-26.el9, zypper install vim=9.0, or bake them into an image pinned by digest Helm helm install/upgrade --version 1.2.3 for a chart outside the scope; a chart in the scope is checked as files Git git clone URL && git -C dir checkout <40-hex>, one checkout per clone; no git pull, no submodule branch = or update --remote Python details
  • Generate the file: uv pip compile --generate-hashes requirements.in -o requirements.txt, then pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt.
  • Once one entry of a requirements file has a hash, every entry needs one.
  • Any requirements*.txt path is checked, also requirements/dev.txt.
  • Poetry needs poetry.lock and Pipenv Pipfile.lock next to the manifest. A pyproject.toml with [project] dependencies needs uv.lock, pdm.lock or poetry.lock, next to it or at the workspace root.
  • A file named by pip install -r/-c, or by an include line inside a requirements file (resolved next to that file), must be in the scope, or it is reported.

docs.title: Container images
docs.text:
Pin every image by digest. Keep the tag for readers; the digest decides.

# compose.yaml, Kubernetes manifests, rendered Helm charts
image: redis:7.4-alpine@sha256:c5d34a98396a4775e223c74e929162c35c5a2182901ba26b50ade939941ce14b

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1@sha256:<digest>
FROM golang:1.25@sha256:<digest> AS build
FROM build AS test          # a stage name is fine
COPY --from=nginx:1.27@sha256:<digest> /etc/nginx /etc/nginx
ADD --checksum=sha256:<sum> https://example.com/tool.tgz /tool.tgz

Find the digest with crane digest <image:tag> or docker buildx imagetools inspect <image:tag>.

What else is checked
  • Images in docker run, podman run, docker compose and kubectl run/create --image commands. A compose file the command uses must be in scope.source; it can be YAML or JSON (compose.json).
  • An image from a variable Aval cannot resolve (${DB_IMAGE}), a Helm template ({{ .Values.image }}), a YAML alias, block scalar or tag (image: *img, image: >-, image: !!str ...) is reported: write the reference inline, or render the chart into the scope.
  • Dockerfiles are read twice. The line pass reads each line as an instruction (continuations joined with a space, RUN heredocs as scripts). The BuildKit pass splits the file as BuildKit does, for files named Dockerfile, Dockerfile.*, *.dockerfile, Dockerfile plus a name without a dot (Dockerfile-dev), and the same with Containerfile: comment lines stand alone, continuations join with nothing between (FROM db:1\ then 6 is db:16), # escape= sets the escape character (continuations and heredoc words), heredoc bodies are kept apart.
  • Both passes treat COPY --from= and RUN --mount=...,from= like a FROM: a stage name or index is fine, an image needs a digest. An instruction behind ONBUILD is checked like the same one without it.
  • The BuildKit pass also reports a file BuildKit refuses (an invalid # escape=, a repeated directive, an unterminated heredoc), a heredoc name with a quote, \ or $, or an empty one, and a FROM image with a variable that is not a global ARG with a value (FROM alpine:$V): give the global ARG a default, or write the image.
  • Kustomize: an images: (or imageTags:) entry with newName or newTag needs a digest:. Reported by name and index (resources[2]): a remote or out-of-scope resources, components or bases entry (vendor it); a patch or replacements entry that sets an image, or is given by an out-of-scope path; a transformers or generators entry with an image transformer or an out-of-scope path; a helmCharts entry, unless the chart is local (no repo, Chart.yaml in the scope under helmGlobals.chartHome, default charts, inside the kustomization directory) and no valuesInline sets an image; any tagSuffix (kustomize drops the digest). An undecodable kustomization is reported by its path. The overlay is not built.
  • YAML is read twice: the line pass matches image: on every line, also inside a block scalar a template renders; the parser matches every key that decodes to image ("ima\x67e":, ? image, !!binary aW1hZ2U=:). A key with another tag, or one the parser cannot decode in a file it rejects, is reported; in *.tpl files, files under templates/ and rejected files, a key a template writes (ima{{ "ge" }}:) is reported by its text, except a range key variable alone ({{ $key | quote }}:) directly under labels: or annotations:. A Compose build.dockerfile_inline is checked as a Dockerfile, and build.additional_contexts values with docker-image:// as images.
  • JSON is read the same way, but only in Compose files, files under templates/ and files a kustomization in scope lists in resources.

docs.title: Scripts from the network
docs.text:
curl … | sh (also through tee), bash -c "$(curl …)", python -c "$(curl …)", eval "$(curl …)", source <(wget …) and releases/latest URLs run or fetch whatever the server sends, also in Dockerfile RUN lines and heredocs. Vendor the script into the scope, or download a fixed version and check its sha256 before running it.

Which files are scanned as scripts

*.sh, *.bash, *.zsh, *.mk, Makefile, and in-scope files without an extension whose first line is a sh, bash, zsh, ksh or dash shebang (./setup). A script with another extension is hashed but not scanned.

docs.title: Resolve a reference instead
docs.text: To follow a tag or branch on purpose, declare it in scope.resolve (Resolve references). That changes the fingerprint when the target moves, but the scanner still reports the reference: pin it or accept it below.

docs.title: Accept a reference on purpose
docs.text:
Sometimes a mutable reference is acceptable, for example an image your team rebuilds and scans every night. Acknowledge it in the contract, with the reason:

apiVersion: aval.trianalab.io/v1
kind: Test
metadata:
  name: orders-integration
runner:
  command: ["docker", "compose", "run", "--rm", "tests"]
scope:
  source: ["**/*.go", "compose.yaml"]
  allowMutable:
    - ref: postgres:16          # exactly as Aval prints it
      reason: rebuilt and scanned nightly; the tag is ours
    - file: deploy/kustomization.yaml   # only the finding in this file
      ref: resources[0]
      reason: vendored upstream base, reviewed on update
cacheability: controlled-environment
  • ref is the text Aval prints: for a missing lockfile, the manifest path (go.mod); quotes in shell commands are dropped. A finding Aval reports because it cannot tell (a templated key, resources[2], a heredoc name, a FROM line) is in the container ecosystem, accepted by its printed ref.
  • file is the path Aval prints before the line number, relative to the contract (runner.command for the command), and limits the entry to that file. Without it, a ref that two files report (resources[0] repeats) is not accepted, and the finding asks for file. With scope.contracts, each contract's entries apply to its own findings.
  • It is part of the contract, so it changes the fingerprint and shows in review.
  • aval run still prints the finding, marked (allowed: <reason>).
Limits

The scanner reads text and is a safety net, not a guarantee; the guarantee is the declared scope and the pins you write.

  • Not detected: unversioned downloads other than releases/latest (curl -o tool URL, curl URL | tar x); Helm values split into repository and tag, or YAML a template prints; a JSON6902 patch file in the scope named by path:; JSON outside the files above; --build-arg values (the ARG default is checked; outside FROM the last value of a name wins); the BuildKit pass on a source file named like dockerfile_test.go.
  • Shell commands are split without a full parser: a quoted ; or > also splits, which can cause needless misses.
  • An option Aval does not know to take a value (tool --opt value install x) hides the subcommand.
  • For the gaps, declare the reference in scope.resolve (url, image) and run aval run --shadow.
